n3-licao-service.enunciado:
Pods are born and die all the time, and each new pod gets a different IP. Nobody can keep track of those IPs. The Service solves this: a fixed address (an IP and a DNS name) that hands each connection to one of the ready pods, chosen by their labels.

apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: loja
spec:
  selector:
    app: loja        # the pods that answer
  ports:
  - port: 80         # the Service port (the extension)
    targetPort: 8080 # the port the program listens on, inside the pod

Where each thing shows up

  • kubectl get svc: the type, the CLUSTER-IP and the ports;
  • kubectl get endpoints loja: the list of pods behind the extension right now (if it says <none>, the selector found nobody, or nobody is ready);
  • the DNS name: loja (in the same namespace), loja.vendas (from another namespace) or loja.vendas.svc.cluster.local (the full name).

Testing from inside

A Service of the default type (ClusterIP) only exists inside the cluster. To test it, get into a pod: kubectl exec POD -- wget -qO- http://loja (in busybox) or curl (in nginx).
n3-licao-service.vidaReal: The company’s fixed phone extension: people move between apartments, the extension stays the same and rings whoever is there.
n3-licao-service.limite: The extension only rings apartments that are ready to answer (readiness); if none is ready, the call is refused, it doesn’t wait on the line.

n3-licao-de-fora.titulo: Coming in from outside the cluster
n3-licao-de-fora.enunciado:
Three ways to reach a Service from outside:

WayHowWhat for
port-forwardkubectl port-forward svc/loja 8080:80 and then http://localhost:8080Testing from your computer, quickly. Only you use it.
NodePorttype: NodePort: opens the same port (30000–32767) on all nodesLabs and environments without a load balancer.
LoadBalancertype: LoadBalancer: the cloud provider gives you an external IP (EXTERNAL-IP column)Production, when each Service deserves its own IP.

Your computer, in this terminal

On this site, the terminal has two worlds: kubectl exec ... -- wget runs inside a pod; a curl typed directly runs on your computer, outside the cluster. From outside, http://loja doesn’t work (the name only exists in the cluster’s DNS): you need one of the entrances above.
n3-licao-de-fora.vidaReal: The extension only works inside the condo. For people out on the street, there’s the intercom at each building (NodePort), the street-side front gate (LoadBalancer) and the temporary passage from your house (port-forward).
n3-licao-de-fora.limite: In the condo, the street-side front gate is a building; in the cloud, the LoadBalancer is a paid service, created by the provider for every Service of that type.

n3-licao-ingress-gateway.titulo: The condo’s front gate: Ingress and Gateway API
n3-licao-ingress-gateway.enunciado:
One LoadBalancer per Service gets expensive. The Ingress puts a single entrance in front of several Services and picks the destination by name (host) and by path:

rules:
- host: praca.kube-learn.local
  http:
    paths:
    - path: /api           # /api and everything under it
      pathType: Prefix
      backend:
        service:
          name: loja
          port:
            number: 80

The routing is done by an Ingress controller (Traefik, NGINX, HAProxy...), chosen by ingressClassName (or by the cluster’s default class: kubectl get ingressclass).

The new way: Gateway API

The most famous controller, ingress-nginx, was retired in 2026. The path the community recommends is the Gateway API, which splits up the roles:

  • GatewayClass and Gateway: the front gate (address and ports), looked after by the platform team;
  • HTTPRoute: each team’s sign (names, paths and even weights, to send 10% of the traffic to the new version: the canary).

In this simulator, the “company DNS” already points the *.kube-learn.local names used in the Ingresses and HTTPRoutes to the right entrance: test with curl http://praca.kube-learn.local/api.
n3-licao-ingress-gateway.vidaReal: Instead of one front gate per company, a single front gate, with a front desk that says: “/loja, block A; blog.condominio, block B.”
n3-licao-ingress-gateway.limite: The front desk doesn’t do anything on its own: it needs a controller installed in the cluster (the person staffing the desk). Without it, the Ingress is just a piece of paper on the wall.

n3-ramal.enunciado: The loja app has 3 pods, but nobody knows where to call. Create a Service named loja that receives on port 80 and delivers to port 8080 of the pods with the label app: loja.
n3-ramal.dica: spec.selector (the labels) and spec.ports: port and targetPort.
n3-ramal.vidaReal: Giving loja a fixed extension that rings any of the clerks.
n3-ramal.limite: The extension doesn’t know whether a clerk is busy: it just spreads the calls around (round-robin).

n3-expose.titulo: Ordering the extension over the intercom
n3-expose.enunciado: Create the loja Service from the terminal, with kubectl expose: port 80, delivering to 8080.
n3-expose.vidaReal: Asking for the extension over the phone, without filling out a form.
n3-expose.limite: expose copies the Deployment’s selector; if the Deployment changes its labels later, the Service doesn’t follow.

n3-dns-namespace.enunciado: The estoque (stock) Service lives in the estoque namespace. From the cliente pod (default namespace, busybox image), fetch its page and tell us the title that appears in the <title>.
n3-dns-namespace.dica: From another namespace, the name is service.namespace. In busybox: wget -qO- http://...
n3-dns-namespace.vidaReal: Calling another company’s extension in the condo: besides the extension, you say which company.
n3-dns-namespace.limite: Knowing the name doesn’t guarantee the call goes through: with a NetworkPolicy (level 8), one company can block the others.

testes.descricao: you called estoque by name with the namespace

msgs.0: you used the name estoque.estoque from inside the pod

n3-target-port.titulo: The extension on the wrong port
n3-target-port.enunciado: The Service exists, the endpoints show up, but every connection is refused. The loja app listens on port 8080 (check the Deployment’s containerPort, or a pod’s logs). Fix the Service.
n3-target-port.dica: port is the Service’s port; targetPort is the pod’s.
n3-target-port.vidaReal: The extension rings the right apartment, but in the wrong room: nobody answers there.
n3-target-port.limite: Here the call is refused right away; in a real program, sometimes something else is listening on that port, and the error gets more confusing.

n3-ramal-mudo.enunciado: This Service is accepted, but kubectl get endpoints loja shows <none>. Compare its selector with the pods’ labels (kubectl get pods --show-labels) and fix it.
n3-ramal-mudo.dica: The selector has to match the pods’ labels.
n3-ramal-mudo.vidaReal: The extension looks for the “lojinha” door plate, but the doors say “loja”: it doesn’t ring anyone.
n3-ramal-mudo.limite: Kubernetes doesn’t warn you that the selector found nobody: the Service is created normally, it just has no endpoints.

n3-porta-nomeada.enunciado: The Service uses targetPort: http (a name, not a number), but no pod has a port with that name. Give the name http to port 8080 of the loja container.
n3-porta-nomeada.dica: In the container’s ports: - containerPort: 8080 + name: http
n3-porta-nomeada.vidaReal: Instead of “room 8080,” the extension asks for “the service room”: if the number changes, the extension is still right.
n3-porta-nomeada.limite: The name has to exist in every pod: a pod without a port by that name is left out of the endpoints.

testes.descricao: the endpoints use the port by name

n3-nodeport.enunciado: Create the loja Service of type NodePort (port 80 → 8080 on the pods) with nodePort: 30080. Then test from your computer: find a node’s IP with kubectl get nodes -o wide and run curl http://NODE-IP:30080 (without kubectl).
n3-nodeport.dica: spec.type: NodePort and, in ports, nodePort: 30080.
n3-nodeport.vidaReal: A numbered intercom at the door of every building: from any building, 30080 calls loja.
n3-nodeport.limite: The ports are high (30000–32767) and stay open on every node: fine for a lab, hard to remember and to protect.

testes.descricao: from outside, through the node, loja answers

n3-loadbalancer.enunciado: Expose loja with a LoadBalancer Service (port 80 → 8080), wait for the EXTERNAL-IP to show up (kubectl get svc -w) and test from your computer with curl. What is the external IP?
n3-loadbalancer.vidaReal: A front gate on the street just for loja, with its own address.
n3-loadbalancer.limite: In the cloud, each LoadBalancer is a resource billed separately; with many Services, an Ingress or a Gateway comes out cheaper.

testes.descricao: loja has a street-side front gate

msgs.1: you tested with curl from your computer

n3-port-forward.enunciado: Without touching any Service, open a passage from port 8080 on your computer to port 80 of the loja Service and call http://localhost:8080 with curl. Which version does loja answer with?
n3-port-forward.vidaReal: A temporary passage from your house straight to loja, without going through the front gate.
n3-port-forward.limite: The passage goes to a single pod (picked at the start), and it disappears when the command stops.

testes.descricao: you reached loja through the passage

n3-headless.enunciado:
The 3 replicas of the banco database (Redis, port 6379) need to find each other one by one, without round-robin. Create a headless Service named banco: with no IP of its own, the DNS returns each pod’s IP.

Check from a test pod: kubectl run t --image=busybox:1.36 -- sleep 3600 and then kubectl exec t -- nslookup banco.
n3-headless.vidaReal: Instead of an extension that spreads the calls around, a list with each apartment’s number: whoever calls picks who to talk to.
n3-headless.limite: Without the extension’s round-robin, the caller has to know how to choose (that’s the case for databases with replicas and for StatefulSets, in level 4).

n3-ingress-caminho.enunciado:
At the food court praca.kube-learn.local, today everything goes to the blog. Add to the Ingress the rule that sends /api (and whatever comes under it) to the loja Service (port 80).

Test from your computer: curl http://praca.kube-learn.local/api and curl http://praca.kube-learn.local/.
n3-ingress-caminho.dica: Another item in paths: path: /api, pathType: Prefix, backend.service.name: loja.
n3-ingress-caminho.vidaReal: A single entrance for the food court: “/api, the loja desk; everything else, the blog.”
n3-ingress-caminho.limite: The path arrives whole at the destination: loja receives /api (and has to know how to answer on it).

testes.descricao: from outside, /api goes to loja and / to the blog

n3-ingress-host.enunciado: Replace the Ingress with two host rules: loja.kube-learn.local goes to the Service loja and blog.kube-learn.local goes to blog (both on port 80, path /).
n3-ingress-host.dica: Two items in rules, each with its own host.
n3-ingress-host.vidaReal: The same front desk serves two addresses: whoever asks for loja goes one way; for the blog, the other.
n3-ingress-host.limite: The name has to reach the front desk (DNS pointing at the Ingress); here the company DNS already does that for you.

n3-gateway.titulo: The sign at the new front gate
n3-gateway.enunciado: The platform team already created the portaria (front gate) Gateway (see kubectl get gateway). Create an HTTPRoute named loja, attached to that front gate, that takes loja.kube-learn.local to the Service loja (port 80).
n3-gateway.dica: spec.parentRefs: [{ name: portaria }], hostnames and rules[].backendRefs.
n3-gateway.vidaReal: The management office already set up the front gate (Gateway); each company just hangs its own sign (HTTPRoute).
n3-gateway.limite: The sign only counts at the front gate it names (parentRefs), and only if that front gate accepts routes from your namespace.

testes.descricao: from outside, through the new front gate, loja answers

n3-canario.enunciado:
Version 1.1 of loja runs in the loja-v2 Service. Change the route to send 90% of the traffic to loja and 10% to loja-v2: the canary.

Test several times from your computer: curl http://loja.kube-learn.local/.
n3-canario.dica: Two backendRefs, each with a weight.
n3-canario.vidaReal: Opening the renovation to 1 in every 10 customers, seeing if anyone complains, and only then to everyone.
n3-canario.limite: The split is per request: the same customer may land on the old version one time and on the new one the next.

testes.descricao: out of 100 customers, about 10 see the new version
